phase: 5 - cold start reads one real resource, twice

target.why_this_file: a real system resource, uncompressed, five blocks, so every byte comes off the flash

where_the_numbers_come_from.counters: three in hakios.xnusys_blk.c: first_ns, reads, blocks_read
where_the_numbers_come_from.note: the user program cannot inflate them; it reads them after the fact

why_45_reads_for_5_blocks: the other 40 are the file system walking its own metadata: container superblock, omap, volume superblock, the fs-tree's interior nodes, the inode and the extent record. That the count stays at 45 across boots shows the cache is doing its job.

independent_mount.what: the volume is mounted at a mount point of its own, /redwood/lib, separate from the ramdisk on /redwood
independent_mount.evidence: mount /dev/xnusys on /redwood/lib -> 0, then stat and getdirentries on that path

early_user_program_read.what: process 1 runs /redwood/bin/xnusys_coldstart out of /redwood/etc/rc, before launchd.ios is exec'd, and reads a real resource through the mount
early_user_program_read.evidence: 19577 bytes, fnv1a bbdbcb6f, matching the host's independent read of the same file

system_volume_switch.what: booting with the APFS volume as the root, instead of the ramdisk
system_volume_switch.why_not: the roadmap makes this conditional: 'if the project actually needs to boot from the volume'. Nothing in stages 1-4 depends on it, and doing it would change what is being tested. Recorded as not done rather than omitted.

roadmap_row: stage 5 asks for an early user program reading a real resource off the mounted volume, with first read, command count and timing recorded, and two independent boots reading the same target. All four are in this record. The system-volume switch is the conditional half.
